title: Jijabai Raises Shivaji
text:
Jijabai was the daughter of a Maratha noble, Lakhuji Jadhav, and the wife of Shahaji Bhosale, a commander who served the sultans of the Deccan. Shahaji spent most of his career far away in the south, in the service of Bijapur, and lived there with another wife. Jijabai raised their younger son, Shivaji, born around 1630, largely on her own.

In the late 1630s she settled with the boy in Pune, on Shahaji's estate. The town had been ravaged by war. With the help of the administrator Dadoji Konddev, she rebuilt it and had the land brought back under cultivation. Maratha tradition remembers her telling Shivaji the stories of the Ramayana and the Mahabharata, of heroes who fought injustice, and teaching him to see himself as the protector of his people and their faith rather than as the servant of foreign sultans.

Shivaji grew up among the hill people of the region and began, as a teenager, to seize forts in the Sahyadri hills. Over the following decades he built an independent Maratha kingdom. Jijabai remained his adviser, and the chronicles describe her as managing affairs when he was away or in danger.

In June 1674 Shivaji was crowned king at Raigad fort. Jijabai lived to see it. She died less than two weeks later.
lesson: The stories a parent tells and the values she lives by can shape a child's whole idea of who he is. Upbringing is the first school of leadership.
people: Jijabai, Shivaji, Shahaji Bhosale, Dadoji Konddev
source: Maratha chronicles (bakhars); Jadunath Sarkar, Shivaji and His Times (1919)
caveat: Much of what is told about Jijabai's teaching comes from later Maratha chronicles and tradition.
